ev.q: The ratio of BLL tests performed among Chicago children aged 11–48 months per 100 children aged <5 years in 2020 (14.7) was 29.1% lower than the annual average during 2017–2019 (20.7)
the decrease in testing was also greater in these highest risk areas (total decrease = 18%; median decrease = 17.7%)
The total number of lead tests performed during March–September was divided by the American Community Survey 5-year population estimate of children aged <5 years.
The average during 2017–2019 was assigned as the prepandemic baseline.
Within each of the three risk categories, the total decrease was calculated as well as the median decrease
The ratio increased during 2021 (17.5) and 2022 (18.5) but remained 15.4% and 10.6% lower than during the 2017–2019 baseline, respectively.
The effect was evaluated geographically by assigning community areas
